checks.detail: Year, month and event match both cited pages.

checks.item: 1886: Goldfield proclaimed and town laid out. Gold found on the farm Langlaagte; President Kruger declared the area open for public diggings on 20 September 1886; town surveyed beside Ferreira's Camp and named Johannesburg.
checks.found: Wikipedia: 'discovery of an outcrop of a gold reef on the farm Langlaagte. September 20 1886 was when President Paul Kruger declared the area ... open for public diggings'; the town 'was laid out on ... Randjeslaagte'; Ferreira 'staked out his camp on Turffontein'. SAHO: mining commissioner Carl von Brandis 'proclaimed the first mining activities on 20 September 1886 on the farm Randjeslaagte'.
checks.detail: Date and event match. The two cited pages differ on who read the proclamation (Kruger's declaration in Wikipedia, read out by commissioner von Brandis in SAHO); the date is the same in both, so nothing was changed.

checks.item: 2010: World Cup final and Gautrain. Rebuilt Soccer City hosted the 2010 FIFA World Cup final; Gautrain, begun in 2006, completed in June 2012.
checks.found: History: 'A completely refurbished Soccer City stadium in Johannesburg hosted the 2010 FIFA World Cup final.' Johannesburg: Gautrain links Johannesburg and Pretoria, and Sandton and OR Tambo airport; 'Construction of the Gautrain Rapid Rail started in October 2006 and was completed in June 2012.'
checks.detail: All parts of the description match the cited pages.

summary: All 10 sampled items matched their cited sources (Britannica 1911, Wikipedia census and timeline pages, tower and bridge articles). Nothing was changed. As a side check after finding floor-count estimates among Bandung's CTBUH heights, the seven CTBUH pages cited for Johannesburg were opened: none is marked as an estimate and all heights and years agree with the file.
